title: Handle a co-founder departure
summary: Three things protect the company: the equity math, a properly authorized decision, and a deadline. Calculate vested versus unvested equity at the departure date. Have the body your governing documents name accept the resignation and authorize what happens to the unvested equity under the founder agreement. Act inside the window that agreement sets; windows lapse, so read yours. Confirm the signed IP assignment is on file. Revoke access the same day. Update the ownership records. Tell the team once, clearly. Separation agreements and releases are work for employment counsel. Once executed, the equity settlement and its authorization cannot be undone. Educational guidance, not legal advice.

metadata.trigger: A co-founder is leaving (resignation or a split) and the vesting, IP, and access mechanics start now.
metadata.supportReason: The authorization and the equity settlement are signature acts with closing windows, and the departure terms are negotiated between people. An agent can run the vesting math, the access revocation, and the cap-table update.

contextNeeded.query: the stock purchase agreement (vesting schedule, repurchase window)

geoNotes.summary: The mechanics run through Companies House (TM01 for the directorship, PSC updates where ownership crosses thresholds) and through the articles and shareholders' agreement — good-leaver/bad-leaver provisions usually decide what happens to the shares and at what price.

GmbH shares move only by notarized deed (§15 GmbHG — the Abtretung requires notarielle Beurkundung) and the updated Gesellschafterliste is filed to the Handelsregister; founder vesting lives in the Gesellschaftervereinbarung, not in statute, so read yours first.

In a SAS the statuts and the pacte d'associés govern the exit (leaver and forced-transfer clauses); the share movement is recorded in the company's registre de mouvements de titres and officer changes file through the INPI guichet unique.

Director changes file to the RoC on DIR-12 within 30 days (the director's own DIR-11 alongside), share transfers move on Form SH-4 with stamp duty, and founder vesting is a shareholders'-agreement matter enforced through the articles — same mechanics, MCA paperwork.

The exit runs through the acordo parassocial's leaver clauses: quota transfers need written form and registration (no notary since 2006), the registry record is updated online, and the vesting/clawback math is whatever the agreement wrote down.

The USA's leaver provisions govern: vested vs unvested shares at the departure date, a directors' resolution for any repurchase, updated share registers — and since 2024 CBCA corporations also file individuals-with-significant-control changes.

The register work runs through the Companies Office: update the departing director's details online and move the share allocations on the register; the equity settlement itself lives in the shareholders' agreement's leaver terms.

geoNotes.summary: The mechanics run through Bizfile (file the director's cessation with ACRA) and through the constitution and shareholders' agreement — leaver clauses decide the shares, transfers attract stamp duty through IRAS e-Stamping, and a private company's register of members only moves when ACRA updates it.

The mechanics run through ASIC and the shareholders' agreement: notify the director ceasing within 28 days (Corporations Act 2001 s 205B(5)), apply the leaver provisions to the shares, and record any transfer or cancellation on the members register with ASIC notified.

The departing founder’s shares move under the shareholders’ agreement; where the articles make transfers subject to board approval (Commercial Act Article 335), the buy-back route is pre-wired, and director changes register on the two-week clock.

The departing founder's shares move under the shareholders' agreement: shares transfer freely to other shareholders by default, third-party transfers carry a one-month pre-emption right, and the articles can require consent (Commercial Code § 149); board changes are registered in the commercial register.
